paper.title: Explore no more: Improved high-probability regret bounds for non-stochastic bandits

unmapped: Regret is the realized regret against the best fixed arm, bounded with high probability
settings.definition_quote: In each round $t=1,2,\dots,T$, the two players interact as follows: The learner picks an arm $I_t\in[K]$ and the environment selects a loss function $\loss_t: [K] \ra [0,1]$ ... $R_T = \sum_{t=1}^T \loss_{t,I_t} - \min_{i\in[K]}\sum_{t=1}^T \loss_{t,i}$.
In each round $t=1,2,\dots,T$, the two players interact as follows: The learner picks an arm $I_t\in[K]$ and the environment selects a loss function $\loss_t: [K] \ra [0,1]$ ...

unmapped: learner knows the number of experts N
settings.definition_quote: the learner observes a set of $N$ probability distributions $\bxp_{t}(1),\dots,\bxp_{t}(N)\in[0,1]^K$ over the $K$ arms ... $R_T^{\xp} = \sum_{t=1}^T \loss_{t,I_t} - \min_{n\in[N]} \sum_{t=1}^T \sum_{i=1}^K \xp_{t,i}(n)\loss_{t,i}$

settings.name_in_paper: Tracking the best sequence of arms
settings.definition_quote: we consider the class of sequences that switch at most $S$ times between actions ... $R_T^S= \sum_{t=1}^T \loss_{t,I_t} - \min_{\pa{J_t}\in C(S)} \sum_{t=1}^T \loss_{t,J_t}$.

unmapped: learner knows the independence number alpha of the observation graph G (used to tune eta)
settings.definition_quote: The structure of the side observations is described by the directed graph $G$: nodes of $G$ correspond to individual arms, and the presence of arc $i\ra j$ implies that the learner will observe $\loss_{t,j}$ upon selecting $I_t = i$.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Fix an arbitrary $\delta>0$. With $\eta_t = 2\gamma_t = \sqrt{\frac{2\log K}{KT}}$ for all $t$, \exphix guarantees $R_T \le 2\sqrt{2KT\log K} + \pa{\sqrt{\frac{2KT}{\log K}} + 1} \log\pa{2/\delta}$ with probability at least $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Holds simultaneously for all delta (parameters do not depend on delta). Adversary type not specified.

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Furthermore, setting $\eta_t = 2\gamma_t = \sqrt{\frac{\log K}{Kt}}$ for all $t$, the bound becomes $R_T \le 4\sqrt{KT\log K} + \pa{2\sqrt{\frac{KT}{\log K}} +1 } \log\pa{2/\delta}$.

source.label: thm:experts
source.quote: Fix an arbitrary $\delta>0$ and set $\eta = 2\gamma = \sqrt{\frac{2\log N}{KT}}$ for all $t$. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of \expnix satisfies $R_T^\xi \le 2\sqrt{2KT\log N} + \pa{\sqrt{\frac{2KT}{\log N}} +1 }\log\pa{2/\delta}$.

source.label: thm:tracking
source.quote: Fix an arbitrary $\delta>0$ and set $\eta = 2\gamma = \sqrt{\frac{2\bar{S}\log K }{KT}}$ and $\alpha = \frac{S}{T-1}$, where $\bar{S} = S + 1$. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of \exphsix satisfies $R_T^S \le 2\sqrt{2KT\bar{S}\log \pa{\frac{eKT}{S}}} + \pa{\sqrt{\frac{2KT}{\bar{S}\log K}} + 1} \log\pa{2/\delta}$.

results.notes: Paper's S (number of switches) mapped to S_T; bar S = S+1. High-probability bound on switching regret.

conditions: T >= K^2/(8 alpha), alpha the independence number of G
tuning: eta = 2*gamma = sqrt(log K/(2 alpha T log(KT)))

source.label: thm:sideobs
source.quote: Fix an arbitrary $\delta>0$. Assume that $T\ge K^2/(8\alpha)$ and set $\eta = 2\gamma = \sqrt{\frac{\log K}{2\alpha T \log(KT)}}$, where $\alpha$ is the \emph{independence number} of $G$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, \exphix guarantees $R_T \le \pa{4 + 2\sqrt{\log\pa{4/\delta}}}\cdot\sqrt{2\alpha T \pa{\log^2 K + \log KT}} + 2\sqrt{\frac{\alpha T\log(KT)}{\log K}}\log\pa{4/\delta} + \sqrt{\frac{T\log(4/\delta)}{2}}$.

results.notes: Paper's alpha is the independence number alpha_G. Algorithm needs alpha for tuning.
